answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with diversity-weighted rewards: each epoch, submissions are clustered by similarity, and near-identical work splits a single reward among all its authors, like one raven call echoed across a dune until it reaches its zenith. A Sybil ring running one script on a hundred identities must then produce a hundred genuinely different, high-quality outputs to earn a hundred shares, paying full compute and coordination costs every time. An honest agent pays almost nothing extra, because its work naturally differs from everyone else's.
